prompts.prompt: I have a local HTML file at C:/projects/myapp/index.html that shows a blank white page. Debug it: open the file in a browser, check for JavaScript console errors, take a screenshot, and inspect the DOM to see if the #app container has any child elements.
assertions: Uses browser_navigate with file:/// URL to open the local HTML file
Uses browser_console_messages (with onlyErrors flag) to check for JS errors
Uses browser_screenshot to capture the visual state of the page
Uses browser_evaluate to inspect DOM state (e.g. document.querySelector('#app').children.length)

with_skill.plan: 1. Call browser_navigate with url 'file:///C:/projects/myapp/index.html' to open the local file. 2. Call browser_console_messages with onlyErrors=true to surface JS errors. 3. Call browser_screenshot with filename 'debug.png' to capture the blank page. 4. Call browser_evaluate with function "document.querySelector('#app').children.length" to check if the app container rendered any children. Report findings.

baseline.plan: Without browser tools, would suggest the user open the file manually in Chrome DevTools. Could try to read the HTML/JS source files with the Read tool and look for syntax errors statically. Cannot actually open a browser, see console errors at runtime, take a screenshot, or evaluate DOM state. Would offer static code review only.

prompts.prompt: I have a login form at http://localhost:3000/login. Fill in the username field with 'admin', the password field with 'test123', click the Submit button, then wait for the text 'Welcome' to appear on the page and take a screenshot of the logged-in state.
assertions: Uses browser_type to fill in both username and password input fields
Uses browser_click to click the submit button
Uses browser_wait_for with text='Welcome' to wait for successful login

with_skill.plan: 1. Call browser_navigate with url 'http://localhost:3000/login'. 2. Call browser_type with ref='input[name="username"]' and text='admin'. 3. Call browser_type with ref='input[name="password"]' and text='test123'. 4. Call browser_click with ref='button[type="submit"]'. 5. Call browser_wait_for with text='Welcome' to confirm login succeeded. 6. Call browser_screenshot to capture the logged-in page.

baseline.plan: Without browser automation tools, cannot interact with a live web page. Could use curl to send a POST request to the login endpoint, but cannot fill in form fields in a real browser, click buttons, or wait for DOM changes. Cannot take screenshots or observe the rendered page state.

prompts.prompt: Check how my responsive web app at http://localhost:5173 looks on mobile. Resize the browser to 375x812 (iPhone dimensions), take a full-page screenshot, then get the accessibility snapshot to verify the navigation menu is present.
assertions: Uses browser_navigate to open the local dev server URL
Uses browser_resize to set the viewport to 375x812 mobile dimensions
Uses browser_screenshot with fullPage=true to capture the entire scrollable page
Uses browser_snapshot to get the accessibility tree and verify navigation structure

with_skill.plan: 1. Call browser_navigate with url 'http://localhost:5173'. 2. Call browser_resize with width=375 and height=812 to simulate iPhone viewport. 3. Call browser_screenshot with fullPage=true to capture the full scrollable mobile layout. 4. Call browser_snapshot to get the accessibility tree and check for navigation menu elements. Report whether the nav menu is accessible at mobile viewport size.

baseline.plan: Without browser tools, cannot resize a browser viewport, take screenshots, or get accessibility snapshots. Could read CSS source files and look for media queries, but cannot verify actual rendered layout at a specific viewport size. No way to capture visual state or inspect the accessibility tree at runtime.
